intro: Competitive skateboarding is judged on how well skaters ride an obstacle course: the tricks they choose, how cleanly they land them, and how they use the space. There are two Olympic disciplines — street, built like an urban plaza with stairs and rails, and park, a bowl of curved transitions. World Skate governs the sport internationally.
inThirtySeconds: Judges score runs and tricks from 0 to 100.
Street: timed runs plus single best-trick attempts.
Park: timed runs in a bowl; the best run counts.
Falling (a 'bail') ruins a trick — landing it cleanly is everything.
objective: Earn the highest score by combining difficult, varied tricks with clean execution and flow.

facts.duration: Runs of about 45 seconds; single-trick attempts
equipment: Helmet (mandatory in some events and age groups)

scoring.label: Run score
scoring.detail: An overall impression of a timed run.

scoring.label: Trick score
scoring.detail: Street only: a single trick attempt on one obstacle.

variants.name: Street
variants.description: A course of stairs, rails, ledges and banks, inspired by city spaces.

variants.name: Park
variants.description: A bowl with deep curved walls for flowing lines and big airs.

bodies.name: World Skate
bodies.scope: International federation for skateboarding and roller sports

rules.title: Judging criteria
rules.summary: Judges consider difficulty, execution, variety, flow and use of the course, plus consistency.
rules.body: Scores are an overall impression rather than a points-per-trick table. The highest and lowest judges' scores are usually discarded. A trick no one has landed before in competition can earn big scores — if it's landed cleanly.

rules.title: Bails and incomplete tricks
rules.summary: A trick only counts if the skater lands and rides away in control.
rules.body: In street best-trick attempts, a bail scores zero. In runs, a fall usually ends the run's momentum and heavily affects the score.

rules.title: Street: runs and best tricks
rules.summary: Skaters get two timed runs and several single-trick attempts; the best run and best trick scores are combined.
rules.body: Exact numbers of attempts and how many trick scores count depend on the event format, so check the competition's rules. Single tricks let skaters attempt their hardest manoeuvres on one feature.

rules.title: Park: best run counts
rules.summary: Skaters have a few timed runs around the bowl, and their single best run is their score.
rules.body: Park rewards height (amplitude), speed and linking tricks in a continuous line through the bowl.

fouls.name: Bail
fouls.description: Falling or failing to ride away from a trick.
fouls.consequence: Zero for the trick / lower run score

fouls.name: Running over time
fouls.description: Tricks after the run timer ends.

flow.title: Practice
flow.description: Skaters learn the course in practice sessions.

flow.title: Runs
flow.description: Timed runs showcase lines and variety.

flow.title: Best tricks
flow.description: Street skaters go for their hardest single tricks.

field.name: Course
field.dimensions: Varies by event; street courses resemble plazas, park courses are bowls
notes: Park: bowls with transitions, coping and vertical walls

glossary.definition: Jumping with the board without using the hands — the foundation of street skating.
Flicking the board to spin it along its length in the air.
Sliding along an edge on the board's trucks.
The metal edge at the top of a bowl wall.

funFacts: Skateboarding began in California in the 1950s when surfers wanted something to ride when the waves were flat.
Olympic skateboarding debuted at Tokyo 2020 with medallists as young as 13.
